findings.title: Normalize email addresses before storing and matching blocks
findings.body: BlockedEmail stores the supplied email unchanged and matches it using an exact, case-sensitive equality query. An entry for `bad@example.com` therefore does not match `bad@EXAMPLE.COM`, although those addresses refer to the same mailbox (domain names are case-insensitive). No normalization is performed by this model or the new validator, so differently cased block entries or registration addresses can evade the block. Normalize both stored entries and lookup values consistently with the application's email handling.

findings.title: Update match statistics atomically
findings.body: The match counter is incremented with an unlocked read-modify-save sequence. If two registration requests match the same blocked email concurrently, both can read the same match_count and save the same incremented value, losing one match. A delayed save can also overwrite a newer last_match_at. Use an atomic database increment/update or lock the record while updating these statistics.
